solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Door on stage previously the way out?

indicators.note: on here means tacked on after, so the door word follows the other two pieces

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
previously means before, earlier in time
a wicket is a small door or gate, often set in a larger one

explanation.surface: A stage direction wondering whether the door previously used on stage was the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cricket: one of the ways a batter can be given out, hence 'the way out?' with its question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batter can be dismissed this way, one of the recognised methods of getting a player out.

clue.text: Chap upset that ladies keep touching the port

indicators.note: keep means hold inside, so the lavatory word encloses the reversed chap

parts.note: the ladies is a women's lavatory, shortened to LAV

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a chap is a male, he
touching means concerning, regarding, i.e. RE

explanation.surface: A man is upset that the ladies' room keeps brushing up against the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' works as a reversal only because this is a down entry; 'keep' is the containment signal, not a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major French seaport at the mouth of the Seine, a harbour city in Normandy.

clue.text: Beth's successor set about that fellow from the East End

indicators.note: about means around, so the set word goes round the cockney pronoun

parts.note: to set, as a jelly does, is to gel

parts.words: that fellow from the East End
parts.note: a Cockney from London's East End drops the H of him, giving 'im

explanation.surface: Someone who followed Beth got a man from the East End to arrange something.
explanation.walkthrough: Beth is not a woman but the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet; the one after it is the third.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Hebrew alphabet beth is the second letter, and this is the third letter, coming straight after it.

clue.text: Spy heading off doesn't quite drain glass

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut away from the phrase that follows

parts.note: someone who doesn't quite drain a glass leaves a drop in it

explanation.surface: A spy who heads off without quite finishing a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' takes the L from LEAVES DROP. 'Spy' is the verb: to listen in secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: To spy on people can mean secretly listening in on their private conversations, like an earwigger.

clue.text: Price offered by inadequately stocked ladies' lingerie section?

definitions.meaning: the price offered by a bookmaker on a bet is the betting chance
a poorly stocked department holds only leftovers

explanation.surface: A cut price offered by a clothing department that has run short of stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker's price on a horse is expressed as betting chances such as five to one.

clue.text: Green nut essence, initially for cake baked specially

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of the word essence
baked specially means the letters of for and cake are cooked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe step: nut essence first, for a cake baked specially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green nut' looks like a recipe ingredient but means an environmental enthusiast; 'nut' is a fanatic.
explanation.definitionFit: A green is an environmentalist and a nut is a fanatic, so this is a zealous environmental campaigner.

clue.text: Son prepared for sacrifice means to save on electricity

parts.note: an ISA (individual savings account) is a British tax-free way to save money
AC, alternating current, stands for electricity

explanation.surface: A son readied for sacrifice is a way to save on the power bill.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a UK tax-free savings account; 'on' just stacks it above AC in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abraham was told to offer his son as a sacrifice before an angel stopped him.

clue.text: Check coastal fortification

definitions.meaning: to check an enemy is to hold them off, keep them at a distance
read literally, a castle keep standing at a bay on the coast

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: a keep (castle tower) at a bay.
explanation.definitionFit: To check an advance is to hold it off and prevent it coming closer, which this idiom expresses.

clue.text: Unrated article by priest with covering letter

indicators.note: covering means the letter's spelling goes around the other pieces

parts.note: the letter T is spelt out as TEE
A is the indefinite article
by means times in multiplication, the sign X
FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: A newspaper article by a priest, sent with a covering letter, goes unrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering letter' looks like one phrase, but 'covering' is the container signal. 'Unrated' means not liable to rates, a British local tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrated escapes local rates, a kind of levy, so it is exempt from duty.

clue.text: One shot in HD — old English movie, bizarrely

indicators.note: bizarrely means the letters gathered here are thrown into a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing an old English film shown in high definition, bizarrely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One shot' means a film one has shot oneself, not a single camera take.
explanation.definitionFit: A family's camcorder recording is a film made by an amateur at home, shot by themselves.

clue.text: Lots of cheers when one's out for a pair

indicators.note: out means the letter for one is removed from the farewells

parts.note: cheers can mean goodbye, and many farewells are adieux
one is I, the Roman numeral; one's here means one is

explanation.surface: Lots of cheering when a pair is out, as at a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' is the British goodbye, not applause; the plural of adieu is ADIEUX.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means for two or between two people, as in a meal for a couple.

clue.text: One's filling so long a bag

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so one's sits within the farewell

parts.note: so long is goodbye, and vale is Latin for farewell
one's is one is: I (one) plus S

explanation.surface: Someone filling a bag for a long trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' stands for 'one is', giving I and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A small travelling case for clothes is a type of bag carried on a journey.

clue.text: Sort of detective maybe having weapon to take charge of

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
to chair a meeting is to take charge of it

explanation.surface: A detective type who carries a weapon and takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: This kind of detective solves crimes from home without legwork; 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a detective works things out by reasoning while seated at home, like Miss Marple or Nero Wolfe.

clue.text: Fellow campaigning to stop endless spin

indicators.note: to stop means to plug, sitting inside the shortened swirl
endless means the final letter is dropped from the swirl word

parts.note: an eddy is a swirl or spin of water
campaigning, as an army does, is waging war

explanation.surface: A man campaigning to put a stop to endless political spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' suggests political messaging, but here it is whirling water; 'to stop' means to plug a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name stands for any fellow, the clue treating a common male name as an example.

clue.text: Label on box of tablets below with a faint pattern

indicators.note: below means the next pieces sit underneath in this down entry
on in a down clue means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a term is a word or label for something
the Ark of the Covenant was the chest holding the stone tablets of the Law

explanation.surface: A label on a pill box, below which is a faint pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Label on box of tablets' gives TERM over ARK; 'below' puts that under W and A. The tablets are Moses's stone ones, not pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes and quality paper carry a faint design that shows when held up to the light.

clue.text: Plain butty and pasty with black filling

parts.note: butty is a dialect word, especially Welsh, for a friend or mate

indicators.note: filling means the letter for black goes inside the pale word

parts.note: a pasty complexion is pale
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A plain meal: a sandwich and a pasty with black pudding inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A butty is also a northern English sandwich and a pasty a pastry, but here they mean mate and pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means obvious or evident, readily perceived, as in a tangible tension in the room.

clue.text: Yank accepting month in gym as alternative to class work?

indicators.note: accepting means taking inside, so the yank word goes round the rest

parts.note: to yank is to pull

indicators.note: in places the month inside the gym abbreviation

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
NOV is the abbreviation for November

explanation.surface: An American taking a month off from the gym to do classwork instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' is not an American but the verb. 'class work' is a classic of literature; the alternative is lurid fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap sensational fiction printed on rough paper is the opposite of a literary classic, a classy work.

clue.text: One covered working person no longer in union

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
taken as written

explanation.surface: A working person who was covered, no longer a member of the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union but means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose marriage has been legally dissolved is no longer joined in wedlock.

clue.text: Tidy up ad for broadcast, having complied with customs

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Tidying up an advertisement before broadcasting it, in line with local customs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'customs' looks like traditions but is the border office collecting import tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods on which import tax has been settled at the border have satisfied the customs authorities.

clue.text: Something snappy, like the start of Caesar's campaign report, abridged?

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the last letter is cut

parts.words: the start of Caesar's campaign report
parts.note: Caesar reported 'veni, vidi, vici': I came, I saw, I conquered, which opens with I came

explanation.surface: A snappy summary, like the opening of Caesar's famous report on a campaign, cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged' cuts I CAME to I CAM. 'Something snappy' is a device that takes snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a photograph, so a device that takes them is a camera, here the digital kind.

clue.text: Affect to make trouble, after seeing Russian coin on Scrabble board?

definitions.meaning: to affect is to pretend, to make a show of doing something

definitions.text: to make trouble, after seeing Russian coin on Scrabble board?
definitions.meaning: seeing ROUBLE on the board, a player adds one letter T in front to make the word trouble

explanation.surface: Someone pretending to cause trouble over a Russian coin in a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: seeing ROUBLE (a Russian coin) on the Scrabble board, you lay down a T tile before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect something is to pretend or feign it, doing it only half-seriously, as children pretend at soldiers.

clue.text: One pinching a small part of one's fortune?

definitions.meaning: a pincher is a thief, someone who steals things

definitions.text: a small part of one's fortune?
definitions.meaning: a fortune-teller reads the soggy leftovers in a teacup to predict the future

explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang this phrase rhymes with thief. Fortunes are told from what is left in a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinching is British slang for stealing, and Cockney rhyming slang uses the phrase for a thief.

clue.text: Force no teacher with kid should back

indicators.note: should back means the assembled pieces are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
SIR is what British pupils call a male teacher
to kid or tease is to rag

explanation.surface: No teacher should back the use of force with a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should back' reads as approval in the surface but signals reading the pieces right to left; 'kid' is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of troops stationed in a town or fort is a military force.

clue.text: Carrying litter home over gorge

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
to pig is to gorge on food

explanation.surface: Carrying the rubbish home across a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' is not rubbish but a brood of piglets; 'gorge' is the verb, not a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sow carrying a litter of unborn piglets is pregnant, described by this farming phrase.

clue.text: Female consultant hearing cases

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the two words hold the name within them

explanation.surface: A female consultant hearing cases, as on a tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like the items being heard but signals that the words encase the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name stands for a female person, an example of the category.

clue.text: Hound one trained in spells, familiarly

definitions.meaning: to hound someone is to pester or harass them persistently
the boy wizard Potter, trained at Hogwarts, known by his first name

explanation.walkthrough: 'familiarly' signals a first name; the wizard is J K Rowling's hero.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound is to pester persistently; the wizard Potter's first name is the familiar way to refer to him.

clue.text: Double issue with some violence

definitions.meaning: a double is an exact likeness, as in the spitting image
to issue forcefully, as saliva or words are ejected from the mouth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' is a noun here: someone's lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's double is their exact image, and to eject from the mouth forcefully fits the second sense.

clue.text: Member following cup that cheers winner

indicators.note: following means the member comes after the tea

parts.note: the cup that cheers is a traditional phrase for tea, and CHA is a slang word for tea
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A member follows the trophy that cheers the winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cup that cheers' looks like a trophy but is the old phrase for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A winner of a title or contest is a champion, shortened informally.

clue.text: Eclipse seen before at any time from French islands

indicators.note: seen before means the eclipse word comes ahead of the next piece

parts.note: to eclipse is to outdo or top, i.e. cap
at any time means ever
de is French for from

explanation.surface: An eclipse seen at any time from French islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eclipse' is the verb to outdo, not an astronomical event.
explanation.definitionFit: This republic is an archipelago of volcanic isles off the West African coast.

clue.text: Turn to high drama, perhaps, causing stress

definitions.meaning: read literally, to turn something into a grand theatrical piece
to stress is to emphasise, to draw attention to something

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the idiom literally, as turning something into a fine piece of theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to emphasise it heavily, which this idiom means: to make much of it.
